# Issue #144: content author package

**50 exact groups / 200 proposed fields**, frozen rows **3151–3200**.
Every group has one selected contemporary sense with scoped French, applicable
IPA, English and Chinese. Exact spellings, grammatical subclasses, row order
and frequency strings are unchanged. CEFR remains unknown. No group is omitted
or annotated; no lookup alias is proposed.

[Readable proposals](review-candidates.md), [groups](groups.json),
[field and usage ledger](field-review.json), [source context](source-context.json),
[exact excerpts](source-excerpts.json), [rights](selected-rights.md),
[notices](NOTICES.md) and [admission status](admission.json) supply the reviewable
author result. [Original proposals](authored/groups.json) are preserved for
separate review. The batch uses 52 fixed first-party French article captures:
50 exact pages plus `la sienne` and `four électrique` support.

The author inspected the actual selected definitions, IPA, French/POS frames
and construction/register restrictions. `sienne/PRO:pos` retains its required
`la sienne` construction and feminine singular agreement. `ciao/ONO` is the
French farewell interjection. `business`, `vexer`, `enculer` and `pipi` retain
their informal, vulgar or childish labels. `souper/VER` retains the captured
Belgium/Canada/Switzerland/Occitania evening-meal restriction. `département`
selects the company unit, excluding an outdated territorial count. `go` selects
the board game. Pronunciation variants are selected explicitly, without
changing frozen spellings.

Raw API responses, request URLs, response headers, literal articles,
contributors, reused rights authorities and all author helpers are archived
outside the repository at
`C:/Users/inthe/IdeaProjects/lexique-d2-140-149/context/author-evidence/issue-144/`.
[Capture metadata](source-captures.json) binds the archive to every selected
span. Two completed contributor chains retain all six main responses and one
support response, named registries, anonymous counts and history attribution.
All requests in this run succeeded; successful captures were retained.

## Checks

- Focused missing-resource check: expected failure at the approved
  resource/admission seam; retained `RED.log` under the task archive.
- `uv run --python 3.14.10 python -B -X utf8 scripts/test_core_batch_144.py`:
  passes exact frozen membership/frequencies, 200 complete fields, fixed raw/API
  equality and spans, grammatical frames, complete contributor continuation,
  applicable language/licence bindings and preserved pending author decisions.
- `reproduce.py` in the task archive: passes byte equality for all nine author
  JSON evidence files using retained fixed sources.
- Final documentation, diff and baseline resource checks are recorded in
  [final verification](final-verification.json).

## Remaining gates

**0 new independently accepted groups / 0 admitted fields.** All 200 fields
await independent quality and selected-span rights review. There are no
unresolved authored field values. Actual combined conversion/notices, native
all-group lookup/save/reopen and learner acceptance have not been run by this
author. Those integration/release gates remain pending; this package does not
close #144 or establish release readiness.

Canonical `core-139-v1` at author start has 2,932 admitted groups / 11,728 fields
and 18 zero-field annotations. No canonical input or saved learner data is
changed by this package. Reuse within this batch is zero. The denominator stays
**4,087 groups**; its 50 groups and 200 fields remain outside admitted coverage
until separate review and integration succeed.

isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Readable proposals](review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in

# Selected source rights: #144 author proposal

The 200 proposed fields retain **CC BY-SA 4.0** for fixed Wiktionnaire
contributions and Lexique adaptations. French definitions are scoped
adaptations; English and Chinese are newly authored explanations of the same
selected French semantics. They are not upstream bilingual quotations. IPA
selects one recorded isolated variant and adds slashes. Project code remains MIT.

The [field ledger](rights.json) records each exact source revision, selected
span, attribution, modification and original-work layer. All entries await a
separate selected-text rights decision. The [original proposals](authored/rights.json)
retain those pending decisions; the author assigns no independent acceptance.

Twenty-seven fixed articles contain Académie française eighth-edition import
markers. The original collective dictionary, **1932–1935**, retains separate
credit. The established [original-work rights evidence](../issue-129/selected-rights.md)
applies [CPI L123-3](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/article_lc/LEGIARTI000006278941/2026-02-20):
seventy years from the January following publication. Using final publication
in 1935 gives **2006-01-01**. That original-work determination does not accept
these new fields or later electronic editorial work. Original author/work
respect remains under [L121-1](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000006278891).
Wiktionnaire and Lexique contribution layers retain CC BY-SA 4.0.

Article-level import markers and reference lists do not identify a selected
sentence's author. The full selected lexical spans and their French/POS frames
are retained in [source excerpts](source-excerpts.json). Literary and news
examples, other-language text, etymologies, images and audio supply no field.
The CFC cartographic definition in `filet`, line 93, is explicitly excluded;
the net definition at line 15 supplies its selected meanings. Bibliographic
references to other dictionaries grant no redistribution right to their prose.

`sienne/PRO:pos` uses the fixed `la sienne` possessive-pronoun definition and
agreement table, with the isolated `sienne` IPA. Its required article and
feminine singular agreement remain readable. No bare-pronoun use or runtime
alias is admitted. `four` uses its cooking-compartment definition plus the
fixed `four électrique` cooking sense. `ciao/ONO` uses only the French informal
farewell frame. `go/NOM` selects the two-player board game, excluding the
separately referenced slang girlfriend and verb definitions.

The retained policy revision **38903168**, DAF8-template revision **22113837**,
CC legal text and Wikimedia Terms are listed with their original capture dates
and reuse origins in [rights.json](rights.json). The template says all or part
was extracted and may have changed; it does not prove sentence authorship.
CC BY-SA sections 2(a), 3(a), 3(b) and 4 allow the recorded sharing/adaptations
with attribution, modification notices, ShareAlike and no added restrictions.
Wikimedia Terms section 7 permits linked article/history attribution and
preserves imported material's separate rights.

The [notices](NOTICES.md), [complete legal text](COPYING), fixed article/history
URLs, complete named contributor chains, returned anonymous counts and original
credits define the author package's obligations. Contributor registries may
include later editors; complete linked histories credit anonymous contributors
without claiming sentence-level authorship. Actual combined materials,
conversion, packaged notices and native verification remain integration-owned.
